tspan.data-tip:
core utilization Share of the machine's time that ran tasks. Low means CPU cores sat idle. Covers only configured worker threads.
`a6e22egreen`: >=75% `e6db74yellow`: 50-75% `ff5f45red`: <50%

critical path dead time Frame time minus the work on the longest dependency chain (critical path): how long that chain sat waiting instead of working. High is an optimisation opportunity; the fix depends on the cause (see the split below): core-bound - add cores if possible, or cut total work; dependency-bound - loosen dependencies or rearrange nodes, often profiler-guided.
`a6e22egreen`: <5% `e6db74yellow`: 5-10% `ff5f45red`: >10%
core-bound Dead time where the chain waited for a free core (every core was busy). Fix: add workers or shorten the chain.
mixed A stretch of dead time with both causes present: some cores free, some work still blocked.
dependency Dead time where the chain waited on an unfinished predecessor, not a busy core. Fix: rearrange nodes, profiler-guided optimisation or shorten the chain.
core-time Total worker-time available in a frame: workers x frame time. 100% the split to the right divides up.
body Core-time spent running your task functors (the actual work), summed over all workers.

framework overhead Core-time the framework spent for internal processing: graph execution, launching tasks, scheduling etc. High means tasks are too fine-grained. Try reducing the number of tasks by moving parallelisation to the higher abstraction layer (graph nodes).
`a6e22egreen`: <=5% `e6db74yellow`: 5-15% `ff5f45red`: >15%
idle Core-time with no task to run (workers parked or spinning). High means the frame can't keep the cores fed. Try splitting long-running nodes or add internal node parallelisation.
frame time Wall-clock length of the frame: first task starting to last task finishing.

critical path The fastest the frame could finish given only task durations and dependencies, with infinite amount of workers and CPU cores. The lower limit for frame time. Can only be improved by loosening dependencies or optimising graph nodes internally.
body Total work in the frame: every task functor's time added up across all workers. Divide by workers for the perfect-parallel floor.
orchestration Time the calling thread spends building the run each frame (binding links, re-arming nodes), off the worker cores.

svg.text: views: click to toggle; cycles relabel; Cone: pick a node
critical dead time, core-bound: cores busy
handoff weld: nodes back to back
critical-path ranking — 200 runs, frame time 16.59 ms
Nodes ranked by expected contribution to the binding critical chain (mean × chain%) — where optimising the frame helps most.

tspan.data-tip: chain % How often this node was on the frame's binding critical chain, across the runs. High = it usually decides frame time.
mean Mean wall-clock duration of this node's bar over the runs.
mean × chain% The ranking key: mean duration times chain share = this node's expected contribution to frame time. The table sorts by this.
dead-in Incoming critical dead time: how long this node sat ready but waiting (for a core or a predecessor) before it ran, on runs where it bound the chain.
slack How far this node could slip without extending the frame (structural float from the critical-path method). 0 = on the critical path, with no room to slip.
P95 95th-percentile duration: the node's near-worst-case time, vs its mean.
